newsitem.title: USA: US House ag chair explores CRP fall-crop extension.
newsitem.headline: US House ag chair explores CRP fall-crop extension.

text.p: The chairman of the House Agriculture Committee was exploring the possibility of a one-year extension of Conservation Reserve Program contracts for farmers with fall-planted crops, an aide said Tuesday.
"He's trying to gauge what level of support there would be for doing something," said press secretary Dave Redmond. "How it will turn out, we don't know."

Smith was responding to concerns by farmers that they would not have enough time for fieldwork if the U.S. Agriculture Department did not accept their bids to keep land in the reserve. USDA has said it will rule on applications by early June.

There was skepticism among some lawmakers whether USDA would be able to keep its promise. Smith, Oregon Republican, referred to obvious disagreement over CRP during a speech to the Commodity Club of Washington.
Contracts on more than 20 million acres of Conservation Reserve land expire this fall.

Smith discussed his concern with Senate Agriculture Committee chairman Richard Lugar, Indiana Republican, a Lugar aide said. Lugar was a long-time advocate of CRP reform and has suggested CRP funding would be jeopardized if USDA did not focus on fragile land during this year's sign-up.
The Lugar aide said nothing was scheduled for action in the Senate Agriculture Committee for a CRP extension.

At USDA, spokesman Jim Petterson said the department wanted to "proceed with the new program without delay. We're confident we can handle CRP with as much success" as the 1996 signup for the new farm program, Petterson said.
Congress would have to act in the next several weeks if it wanted to provide an extension. Winter wheat is planted in the fall. Farmers need time in advance to line up equipment, fuel and seed.
